2_Introduction: The device shows the highest PCE of 18.4666% with a VOC of 1.0785 V, a JSC of 22.877 mA/cm², and an FF of 74.8429%. The perovskite composition of Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.8Br0.2 was prepared with a concentration of 1.5 mol/L. The perovskite solution was deposited on the substrate and spun cast at 1000 rpm for 10 s followed by 4700 rpm for 30 s. 200 µL CB was dropped onto the substrate at the last 8 s of the spin-coating, resulting in the formation of dark brown films. By subjecting the film to 110 °C for 30 min, the perovskite lattice attained its ideal orientation.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₁FA₀.₉PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂ perovskite layer—featuring a mixed A-site cation (Cs⁺ enhancing phase stability and suppressing halide segregation, FA⁺ enabling near-ideal Goldschmidt tolerance factor ~0.98 and optimal bandgap ~1.58 eV), Pb²⁺ at the B-site ensuring strong orbital overlap for high carrier mobility, and mixed I⁻/Br⁻ anions tuning lattice strain and defect energetics—undergoes kinetically controlled crystallization wherein the 1.5 mol/L precursor concentration balances nucleation density and growth rate, while the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film uniformity followed by 4700 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent removal) establishes a transient supersaturation gradient that, when precisely interrupted at 8 s with 200 µL chlorobenzene antisolvent, triggers instantaneous nucleation across the substrate without premature aggregation or dewetting; this temporal precision in antisolvent quenching suppresses intermediate solvate phase persistence and minimizes PbI₂-rich grain boundaries, as corroborated by XRD showing complete absence of residual PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6° and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection—indicative of low microstrain, high crystallinity, and suppressed lattice disorder—while optical and PL mapping reveal spatially homogeneous dark-brown film coverage with >98% continuity and uniformly elevated PL intensity and monoexponential decay kinetics (τₐᵥₑ ≈ 380 ns), directly evidencing nanoscale suppression of non-radiative recombination centers and uniform charge-carrier diffusion pathways across the full active area; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 30 min drives complete ligand expulsion, promotes [001]-oriented crystallographic alignment through directional Ostwald ripening, and heals point defects via halide redistribution, collectively yielding optimized interfacial energetics, reduced trap-assisted recombination, and balanced electron/hole extraction—culminating in VOC = 1.0785 V, JSC = 22.877 mA/cm², FF = 74.8429%, and PCE = 18.4666%.
